title: A Very Very Very Dark Matter - review
transcript: the world premiere of a very very very dark matter starring Jim Broadbent at Bridge Theatre London before I review this comedy I'd like to give you some background the inspiration for this story is 19th century Europeans attitude to their colonies which they saw as resources to be exploited to enrich the West all very very very interesting I'm sure you're thinking but the question is is a very very very dark matter any good here's my review a very very very dark matter is a very very dark and also very very very funny Hans Christian Andersen is portrayed as an egocentric idiot and it's clear from the start that the true writer of his terrifying tales is a woman from the Congo who he calls Marjorie and keeps in a cage pants loves the public's adulation but at public readings of his supposed works he can't even pronounce some of the words Jim Broadbent's performance is a comic tour-de-force Marjorie is far more intelligent erudite and sensitive than him a newcomer ginetto EULA Mae Atkins has a quiet Authority that complements Jim Robin's jolly but insecure bastard together they are Jeeves and Wooster for our modern times and this pair are as funny as G's in Worcester of the less actual fun given our acute awareness of humanity's heart of darkness there are many hilarious moments so perhaps the best of which is when hands for pants visits Charles Dickens or Charles Darwin as he insists on calling him he suspects that Dickens too as a ghost writer from the Congo Anderson can't comprehend even the most explicit insults directed at him and the language is both modern every course mr. and mrs. Dickens wonderfully played by Phil Daniels and Elizabeth Barrington exhibit a shocking but no doubt significant contempt for their children they don't even know their names and a Fleischer set is a superb attic full of dark corners and hanging puppets I can't praise the comedy or the production enough if there is a fault it's that it's a bit light on plot I would have liked have been more excited about the fate of Margery and about whether Hance learns from his experience but I give a very very very dark matter four stars if you've enjoyed this review please subscribe to my channel one minute theater reviews by clicking on the icon at the bottom of the screen you
